newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mixed Australian stocks dip at opening.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Australian stocks dip at opening.

text.p: The Australian share market was mixed at the opening on Thursday with miners marginally firmer on the back of buoyant base metal prices while the industrial sector dipped with the Dow.
The All Ordinaries index was down 2.0 points at 2,436.2.
Brokers said market looked set to lose a little ground after Wednesday's strong gains as profit takers moved in.
"It's a little mixed after the U.S. moves," said a Sydney broker. "Metals prices are aiding the miners but there is not great volumes going through."
The early feature came from the smaller end, with Dragon Mining shares rising another 30 percent to A$0.219 (US$0.17) before sellers emerged to force a retreat back to square.
"Dragon is doing the business again but it has come off the top and you may see some sellers come in now," the broker said.
On Wednesday, the junior explorer announced a nickel find at its 35 percent-owned Weld Range prospect in Western Australia.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 10 to nine while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
